requirements.evidence: Data model matches the contract: entities slug unique 'entities_slug_unique' + softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:16-18); memberships with cascade FKs, role default 'employee', stored generated owner_seq and unique indexes 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' / 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (create_entity_memberships_table.php:15-21). Models/enum/factories match the contract (Entity.php:20-52, EntityMembership.php, UserRole.php:420-423, EntityMembershipFactory.php:633-652). Policies follow the rules (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:24-37). Middleware handles 403/0/1/>1 cases (EnsureCurrentEntity.php:45-82); /home dispatches (routes/web.php:21-38); pick checks membership, logs to audit and redirects (web.php:52-67); CreateEntity retries on insert-time unique violation, calling uniqueSlug() every attempt (CreateEntity.php:125-150), logs 'Entity created' and sets the session; switcher markup matches spec (switcher.blade.php:9-13); navbar link only when >1 membership (default-page.blade.php:14-16); lang keys in both locales. Minor gaps: middleware with one membership whose entity is missing continues without a tenant context (EnsureCurrentEntity.php:73-79); the Dashboard's update requests are not covered by current_entity because it is not registered as persistent middleware.

conventions.evidence: The domain write 'Entity::create(...)' + 'memberships()->create(...)' sits inside the Livewire component (CreateEntity.php:130-142) and not in an app/Actions/CreateEntity class, which the conventions require. Business logic for /home, switcher and pick is written as route closures in routes/web.php:21-67, and authorization in pick is an inline 'membershipFor(...) === null -> abort(403)' (web.php:55-57) when it should go through EntityPolicy::view. current_entity is not registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware (Livewire policy rule 6). Followed: #[Validate] + $this->validate() (CreateEntity.php:113,118), $fillable set (Entity.php:250, EntityMembership.php:306), reversible down() in migrations, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md updated, existing <x-form-field>/<x-button> components reused.

security.evidence: CreateEntity authorizes 'create' (CreateEntity.php:120) and always sets role Owner with user_id = auth()->id() server-side, so the client cannot change them (CreateEntity.php:136-139). Dashboard authorizes 'view' in mount (Dashboard.php:216), so a non-member gets 403 even with a valid session for another entity. Pick checks membership before it touches the session (web.php:55-59). All output uses {{ }}. Gaps with limited impact: the custom current_entity middleware is not persisted for Livewire update requests (rule 6), and onboarding entity creation has no rate limit. 'user_id' and 'entity_id' in $fillable are only assigned server-side.

tests.evidence: The diff has no test files at all (no tests/ paths in change.diff). Migrations, policies, middleware, onboarding, pick, switcher, dashboard and navbar changes ship untested. That breaks the 'No production code without a test' rule and the Livewire definition of done (unauthorized-call and tamper tests).

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct code. Duplication: the 0/1/>1 membership dispatch appears twice, in EnsureCurrentEntity.php:63-82 and in the /home closure (web.php:22-37). The 'owner or admin' check is repeated in EntityPolicy.php:498-501 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:448-451,464-467. isUniqueViolation() matches error-message strings and SQLSTATE codes by hand (CreateEntity.php:181-188) when Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException already covers this. '$membership->entity ?? Entity::findOrFail(...)' (web.php:32) is redundant.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, the classes are small and PHPDoc generics match the sibling style (Entity.php, User.php:376-397). Two things are harder to read: the 'while (true)' retry loop with an attempts counter (CreateEntity.php:122-150), and route files that carry real logic in closures (web.php:21-67). There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, migrations, policies, middleware alias (bootstrap/app.php:558-560), routes, views, lang keys, schema docs and CHANGELOG. No out-of-scope pages (members/settings), locale middleware or navbar redesign.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the change, which breaks the project's mandatory TDD rule and the Livewire definition of done (happy path, validation failure, unauthorized and tamper tests).
The entity and owner membership are created directly in the Livewire component; domain writes must go through an app/Actions class that also authorizes.
entity.pick authorizes with an inline membershipFor()/abort(403) check in a route closure instead of a policy (EntityPolicy::view via authorize/can middleware).
The custom current_entity middleware is not registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware, so it stops applying on Dashboard's /livewire/update requests (Livewire policy rule 6).
The 0/1/>1 membership dispatch logic is duplicated between the /home closure and the middleware.
The unique-violation check matches exception message strings and codes by hand; catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException would be simpler and more reliable.
With one membership whose entity no longer resolves, the middleware stores the session and continues without a tenant context; it does not fail clearly.
Entity creation has no rate limit, so a user can create entities in a loop.
'$membership->entity ?? Entity::findOrFail(...)' is redundant; the relation alone (or findOrFail alone) is enough.

review.summary: The change implements the entities data model with a DB-enforced single owner, the policies, the current_entity middleware, onboarding with slug-collision retry, /home dispatch, the switcher, pick and the dashboard, and it updates the docs and CHANGELOG, mostly matching the contract. It ships no tests at all, which the project's TDD rule makes a blocker. It also skips the Actions pattern for domain writes, authorizes pick inline rather than through a policy, and puts dispatch logic in duplicated route closures, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
